propositions.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. Its endomorphisms x,y,h satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y and xy−yx=h. The vector v∈V is nonzero and satisfies xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an arbitrary free abelian subgroup with an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and M is stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! (r∈N). The induced x,y,h actions on V(K)=M⊗_Z K are the actions in the target.

For i=0,…,λ, the vectors e_i=y^iv/i! form a complex basis of V. They satisfy xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For every r≥0, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise.

For i,j∈{0,…,λ}, let E_ij be the complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k≠j to zero, and put c_j=binom(λ,j), A_ij=X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j), and D=∏_(t=0)^λ c_t. Each A_ij preserves M, A_ij=c_jE_ij, A_ij A_kl=δ_(jk)c_j A_il, and D Id_V=Σ_(i=0)^λ(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii.

propositions.statement: For every j with 0≤j≤λ the integer c_j=binom(λ,j) has nonzero image in K; for every r with 0≤r≤λ the integer r! has nonzero image in K. Hence D=∏_(j=0)^λ c_j also has nonzero image in K.

Let A_ij^K denote the operator induced by A_ij|_M on U=M⊗_Z K and define F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1) A_ij^K for 0≤i,j≤λ. Then F_ij F_kl=δ_(jk)F_il and Σ_(i=0)^λ F_ii=Id_U. For 0≤r≤λ the induced divided powers satisfy (r! in K)X_r^K=(x^K)^r and (r! in K)Y_r^K=(y^K)^r.

argument.text: By H001, λ is nonnegative, so natural bounds use λ.toNat=λ and n=λ+1. For every natural i, induction gives h y^i v=(λ−2i)y^i v: at i=0 this is hv=λv; if it holds at i, then hy^(i+1)v=(yh−2y)y^iv=(λ−2i−2)y^(i+1)v. Independently, x y^i v=i(λ−i+1)y^(i−1)v for i≥1. At i=1, xyv=yxv+hv=λv. Assuming this formula at i≥1, the preceding h formula gives xy^(i+1)v=(yx+h)y^iv=[i(λ−i+1)+λ−2i]y^iv=(i+1)(λ−i)y^iv. Both induction assumptions are discharged in their steps. Iterating the x formula for 0≤i≤λ gives x^iy^iv=i!·∏_(t=0)^(i−1)(λ−t)v. Every factor is a positive integer in C for i≥1 in this range; for i=0 the scalar is one. Since v≠0, y^iv and e_i are nonzero. Dividing the first formula by i! gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

produces.statement: For every natural q, hy^qv=(λ−2q)y^qv; for q≥1, xy^qv=q(λ−q+1)y^(q−1)v. For 0≤q≤λ, e_q≠0 and he_q=(λ−2q)e_q.

argument.text: To test independence, fix arbitrary a and temporarily assume L1: Σ_(i=0)^λ a_i e_i=0. For arbitrary j in the range apply ∏_(k=0,k≠j)^λ(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). The h-eigenvector formula F001 makes all summands except j vanish. The remaining equation is a_j ∏_(k≠j)2(k−j)e_j=0. Every 2(k−j) is nonzero in C because k≠j, and e_j≠0 by F001; hence a_j=0. This also covers λ=0, when the operator product is the identity. Discharge L1: a zero linear combination has all coefficients zero. Since a and j were arbitrary, the indexed family (e_i)_(0≤i≤λ) is complex linearly independent.

produces.statement: The family (e_i)_(0≤i≤λ) is complex linearly independent.

argument.text: Apply M001 with scalar field C, ambient space V, finite index type {0,…,λ}=Fin n, and vector family e restricted to that index set. H002 supplies dim_C V=λ+1 and finite dimension; H001 gives n=λ+1, so the number of indices is its dimension. F002 supplies independence. M001 yields span_C{e_i:0≤i≤λ}=V, hence these independent vectors form a basis.

argument.text: Set z=y^(λ+1)v and expand z=Σ_(i=0)^λ b_i e_i using F003. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Subtracting this from the h-action on the expansion and using independence gives 2(λ+1−i)b_i=0 for each i≤λ. This scalar is nonzero in C, so every b_i=0 and z=0. All further y powers on v vanish. From F001 and the definitions, xe_0=0 and xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; directly from factorials ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, while z=0 gives ye_λ=0. Together with the h formula these are all asserted generator actions.

argument.text: For every 0≤i≤λ and r≥0, repeated use of F004 gives x^r e_i=[(λ−i+r)!/(λ−i)!]e_(i−r) if r≤i, and zero if r>i because x kills e_0. Similarly y^r e_i=[(i+r)!/i!]e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ, and zero past the top endpoint because y kills e_λ. These products follow by induction on r, starting with the empty product and multiplying the next coefficient at each step. Divide by r! in C, which is nonzero. Apply M005 first to its natural parameters (λ−i+r,r) when r≤i and second to (i+r,r) when i+r≤λ; the second parameter is at most the first in both cases. The identity choose(N,r)r!(N−r)!=N! identifies the respective scalar ratios as binom(λ−i+r,r) and binom(i+r,r). Thus the X_r,Y_r formulas hold with exactly the zero cases stated in the output statement. F003 and F004 supply its other clauses.

argument.text: Use the basis in N001 to define E and set Q=Y_λX_λ. The divided-power formulas give X_λe_k=0 for k<λ and X_λe_λ=e_0, while Y_λe_0=e_λ. Hence Q=E_(λλ). For every i≤λ, X_(λ−i)e_λ=e_i since its coefficient is binom(λ−λ+(λ−i),λ−i)=1; therefore X_(λ−i)Q=E_(iλ). For every j≤λ, QY_(λ−j) kills inputs e_k with k<j because they land below λ, kills inputs with k>j by termination, and sends e_j to binom(λ,λ−j)e_λ=c_j e_λ. Here binom(λ,λ−j)=binom(λ,j), as seen from the identical factorial ratios λ!/[j!(λ−j)!]. Thus QY_(λ−j)=c_jE_(λj).

By D006 and F001, for all i,j in the index set A_ij=X_(λ−i)QY_(λ−j)=c_j E_ij. By H003 every divided power factor in this expression belongs to U_Z and preserves M, and a composition of maps preserving M preserves M. Thus each A_ij preserves M; this uses no assertion that E_ij itself preserves M.

argument.text: Evaluation on the basis gives E_ijE_kl=δ_(jk)E_il and Σ_i E_ii=Id_V. Using F002, A_ijA_kl=c_jc_lδ_(jk)E_il=δ_(jk)c_j A_il. Also Σ_i(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii=Σ_i(∏_t c_t)E_ii=D Id_V. These use only integer coefficients. Empty products equal one, so the calculation also covers λ=0. Together with F002 these prove every clause of the output statement.

For every natural r≤λ, H001 gives r<p. Apply M004 with ring K, its characteristic p from H001, and source natural n=r. The right side of its equivalence holds, so r! cast into K is a unit and hence nonzero in the field K. This includes r=0, whose factorial is one.

argument.text: For every natural j≤λ, apply M005 with source n=λ.toNat and k=j. Cast its identity c_j j!(λ−j)!=λ! into K. Since λ! is nonzero by F001, the left side is nonzero; if c_j had zero image its product would be zero. Thus every c_j has nonzero image. A finite product of nonzero elements of a field is nonzero, by induction on the number of factors and the absence of zero divisors. D is precisely that product, so its image is nonzero. This proves the output statement with the factorial statement F001.

argument.text: H003 gives stability under every X_r,Y_r. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M; N002 gives stability under every A_ij. Each is complex linear, so its restriction to the additive subgroup M is integer linear. Every identity involving these operators, their compositions and integer scalar multiples restricts to M by pointwise equality in V. In particular the N002 multiplication and diagonal identities restrict, and the defining divided-power identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r restrict for all natural r. No action on a tensor product is used before this preservation is established.

produces.statement: All X_r,Y_r,x,y and A_ij preserve M and restrict to integer-linear endomorphisms. On M, A_ijA_kl=δ_(jk)c_j A_il and D Id=Σ_i(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii for indices in 0,…,λ, and r!X_r=x^r, r!Y_r=y^r for every natural r.

argument.text: Instantiate M003 over Z→K with the integer module M and the endomorphisms in F001. Obtain ρ. Instantiate M007 with tensor factors M,K to obtain σ. Although M007 only asserts additivity, σ is K-linear for the actions in use: for every pure tensor m⊗a and scalar b∈K, σ(b·(m⊗a))=σ(m⊗ba)=ba⊗m=b·σ(m⊗a). Extend this equality by additivity since pure tensors span, and likewise for its inverse. For any integer endomorphism t of M, conjugating ρ(t) by σ gives on m⊗a precisely t(m)⊗a. Thus this conjugate is exactly the D009 induced map whenever t is a restriction in F001. On pure tensors, ρ respects addition, composition and identity; for instance ρ(s)ρ(t)(a⊗m)=a⊗s(t(m)) and ρ(Id)(a⊗m)=a⊗m. Equality holds on all tensors by their finite-sum presentations. Integer scalar multiples also extend to the same integer cast in K by balancing, including negative integers by additivity. Conjugation preserves these identities. Consequently T↦T^K for the lattice maps in F001 preserves their sums, products, identity, integer scalars and powers.

produces.statement: Restriction to M followed by tensor extension sends any integer-coefficient identity involving x,y,X_r,Y_r (r natural) and A_ij (0≤i,j≤λ) to the same identity between their induced K-linear maps on U. It preserves sums, compositions, integer scalar multiples, identity and powers, with T^K(m⊗a)=T(m)⊗a for each such lattice map T.

argument.text: By N003 all c_j and D have nonzero images in K; their inverses therefore exist. Define F as stated. Transfer the N002 identities by F002. For all 0≤i,j,k,l≤λ, F_ijF_kl=c_j^(-1)c_l^(-1)δ_(jk)c_j A_il^K=δ_(jk)c_l^(-1)A_il^K=δ_(jk)F_il. The transferred diagonal identity is D Id_U=Σ_i(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii^K, with coefficients now cast to K. Since D=c_i∏_(t≠i)c_t and c_i,D are nonzero, D^(-1)∏_(t≠i)c_t=c_i^(-1). Multiplying the transferred identity by D^(-1) gives Σ_i F_ii=Id_U. These conclusions are valid when λ=0 as well.

produces.statement: For every 0≤i,j,k,l≤λ, the family F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1)A_ij^K satisfies F_ijF_kl=δ_(jk)F_il, and Σ_(i=0)^λ F_ii=Id_U.

argument.text: Finally apply F002 to the two divided-power identities in F001. For every 0≤r≤λ this gives (r! in K)X_r^K=(x^K)^r and (r! in K)Y_r^K=(y^K)^r. No division by a factorial is used in transferring them. These identities and F003 are the complete output statement.

applications.bindings: Base ring=Z; extension algebra=K via integer cast; source and target integer modules=M. For each integer endomorphism t of M use the base-change map on K⊗_Z M.

H003 gives M as an additive subgroup, with its integer module structure; both source and target are M.
F001 proves that every restricted operator being extended is integer linear. S002 checks preservation of all operations used in the transfer on pure tensors.

H003 gives the integer module M; H001 gives K as an additive commutative group and its integer module structure. S002 proves the extra K-linearity needed for conjugation.

argument.text: H001 identifies λ with its natural value and gives n=λ+1>0. Let ι=Fin n. By H003 an integer basis of M is also a complex basis of V. H002 says V has finite complex dimension λ+1=n. Therefore the index set of that supplied basis is finite with exactly n elements, and it can be relabelled by ι. This is the defining basis-cardinality characterization of finite dimension: any complex basis of an n-dimensional complex space has n elements. Thus there exists an integer basis of M indexed by ι which is a complex basis of V.

produces.statement: There exists an integer basis of M indexed by ι=Fin n, also a complex basis of V, and n=λ+1>0.

argument.text: Choose such a basis b using F001 and H003. Its integer span is all of M and its integer coordinates are unique. The identity of this choice is private to this proof; only its scalar extension and cardinality will be used.

produces.statement: b is an integer basis of M indexed by ι=Fin n.

argument.text: Apply M002 to the base ring Z, canonical Z-algebra K and the integer basis b from F002, obtaining the K-basis B of K⊗_Z M with B_i=1⊗b_i. Apply M007 to obtain σ. It is K-linear: for all m∈M,a,d∈K, σ(d·(m⊗a))=da⊗m=d·σ(m⊗a), and pure tensors span. The same calculation applies to the inverse. Thus σ is a K-linear equivalence for the K-action in D008.

produces.statement: B is a K-basis of K⊗_Z M indexed by ι, and σ:U→K⊗_Z M is a K-linear equivalence sending m⊗a to a⊗m.

argument.text: Define bK_i=σ^(-1)(B_i)=b_i⊗1. F003 implies this is a K-basis of U: apply σ to finite linear relations for independence, and pull back expansions in B for spanning. Apply M006 to field K, vector space U, index type ι and basis bK. It gives dim_K U=Nat.card ι=n=λ+1. This finite basis also proves finite dimensionality. Since n>0 by F001, the index 0 exists and its basis vector bK_0 is nonzero, so U≠0. This proves both clauses of the output statement; the conclusion is independent of the chosen b.

hypothesis_checks: Z is commutative; H001 gives a field K with its canonical Z-algebra structure.
F002 proves b is an integer basis of the additive integer module M, with index ι.

H003 supplies the integer module M and H001 the field K with its additive integer module; S003 verifies K-linearity from the pure-tensor formula.

Use the family from N004, F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1)A_ij^K.

argument.text: N007 establishes that x,y,h and every X_r,Y_r preserve M and have integer-linear restrictions, so every one of their induced operators in D009 is defined. N004 supplies A_ij^K and the family F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1)A_ij^K. N003 supplies the nonzero coefficients in this formula. By H001 the indices 0≤i,j≤λ have λ−i,λ−j,λ all within 0,…,λ.

produces.statement: The induced x,y,h,X_r,Y_r are well-defined on U for every natural r. For all 0≤i,j≤λ the three orders λ−i, λ, λ−j in A_ij lie between 0 and λ.

argument.text: Fix W and introduce L1: W is invariant under x^K,y^K,h^K. Invariance under x^K and y^K implies invariance under every power of these operators, by induction on the exponent with identity as base and composition as step. For each 0≤r≤λ, N003 gives r!≠0 in K, and N004 gives X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)(x^K)^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)(y^K)^r. A K-subspace is closed under scalar multiples, so it is invariant under all these X_r^K,Y_r^K.

produces.statement: W is invariant under X_r^K and Y_r^K for every 0≤r≤λ.

argument.text: For every i,j in the range, D006 and the induced tensor formula imply A_ij^K=X_(λ−i)^K Y_λ^K X_λ^K Y_(λ−j)^K. Indeed the right side applied to a pure tensor m⊗a is (X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j)m)⊗a, the defining action of the left side; N007 guarantees every intermediate lattice vector stays in M, and pure tensors span U. F001 and F002 therefore show W is invariant under A_ij^K. Scalar closure then shows W invariant under F_ij=c_j^(-1)A_ij^K. The h-invariance premise has no further use.

produces.statement: W is invariant under every F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1)(X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j))^K for 0≤i,j≤λ.

argument.text: Discharge L1. For the arbitrary K-subspace W, invariance under the induced x,y,h therefore implies invariance under all the displayed F_ij. Universal introduction in W proves the output statement exactly, with all induced maps already constructed in S001.

Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W⊂U.

argument.text: H001 and D001 give n=λ+1≥1, so the integers 0,…,λ correspond bijectively to Fin n. Reindex the N004 family by this bijection, obtaining F. N004 gives F_ijF_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0) and Σ_i F_ii=Id_U; equality of indices and finite sums are preserved by this bijection. N005 gives dim_K U=λ+1=n and U≠0, and hence finite dimensionality. N007 gives integer restrictions of x,y,h, so the induced actions mentioned in the conclusion are defined and are exactly D009's operators on U.

produces.statement: U is a nonzero finite-dimensional K-space with dim_K U=n. The K-linear family F indexed by Fin n satisfies F_ijF_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0) for all i,j,k,l∈Fin n and Σ_(i∈Fin n)F_ii=Id_U. The induced x,y,h are defined on U.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary K-subspace W and introduce L1: W is invariant under the induced x,y,h. Apply N006 to W. Its operators are the same F as here because N006 and N004 give the identical expression (c_j in K)^(-1)(X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j))^K; reindexing does not change the maps. Therefore W is invariant under every F_ij. Apply E001 with its field=K, space=U, natural parameter=n, operator family=F and subspace=W. H001 gives the field, F001 gives finite dimension n and both matrix-unit identities, and the preceding application of N006 gives invariance. E001 yields W=0 or W=U.

Discharge L1 and universally quantify W: every K-subspace invariant under the induced x,y,h is zero or U. Combine with the nonzero assertion in F001 and U=M⊗_Z K=V(K). H001 allowed every field of characteristic p and every 0≤λ<p. No step requires algebraic closure or distinct weights in K. When λ=0 the index set has one element; when p=2 the permitted λ are 0,1 and the same argument applies. This is exactly P, with the original induced action.

applications.bindings: Source field=K, source space=U=M⊗_Z K, source n=λ.toNat+1, source F=the N004 family reindexed by Fin n, and source W=the arbitrary subspace W in this step.
hypothesis_checks: H001 makes K a field; F001 gives finite dimensionality of U.
D001 makes n natural; F001 gives dim_K U=n.
N004 and the explicit reindexing in S001 give K-linear maps with F_ijF_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0).
N004 gives the diagonal identity, preserved by the reindexing in S001 and recorded in F001.
W is a K-linear subspace by its arbitrary introduction; under L1, N006 applied in S002 gives invariance under precisely this family.

argument.text: For every natural r, X_r and Y_r belong to the subalgebra U_Z by its definition as the integer algebra generated by all these operators. H003 says M is stable under this algebra, so X_r(M)⊆M and Y_r(M)⊆M. In particular, since 1!=1, X_1=x and Y_1=y; thus x,y preserve M.

produces.statement: For every natural r, X_r and Y_r preserve M. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M.

argument.text: H002 identifies the given endomorphism h with xy−yx. For every m∈M, F001 places x(y(m)) and y(x(m)) in M; since M is an additive subgroup, their difference is in M. Therefore h(M)⊆M. Every listed complex-linear map is additive and respects integer multiples; its restriction to M is consequently an integer-linear endomorphism. This proves the output statement without using any induced operator or assuming any further hypothesis.
